en.summary: Replit has launched Monitoring Agent, a monitoring agent that serves as an autonomous on-call engineer for apps. It reads production logs and metrics to investigate errors, slowdowns, and failed deployments; with autofix enabled, it verifies fixes and reports back by email, and with auto-publish enabled it can deploy fixes automatically. The capability builds on the earlier App Monitoring launch, and users can turn it on in an app's Publishing settings.
en.reason: Replit's Monitoring Agent reads production logs and metrics to investigate errors, slowdowns and failed deployments, verifies fixes with autofix enabled, emails reports, and can auto-deploy repairs via auto-publish when switched on in an app's Publishing settings.

en.summary: Claude officially announced that starting next week, sessions on the Pro, Max, and Team plans across the Claude web, desktop, and mobile apps will run in auto mode by default. Auto mode no longer asks for user approval at each step; instead, automated checks block high-risk actions, and users can switch back to manual mode at any time. The Claude Code update it cites notes that auto mode uses a separate classifier to review shell commands, intercepting 89% of dangerous commands in testing, compared with 14% for manual approval.
en.reason: Next week, Claude's Pro, Max, and Team sessions on web, desktop, and mobile default to auto mode, whose classifier blocked 89% of dangerous shell commands in tests versus 14% under manual approval, with users able to switch back.

en.summary: In a long-form retrospective, Newcomer traces Anthropic’s equity evolution from an OpenAI breakaway team to an imminent IPO. Anthropic had explicitly told investors it would cap any single investor’s stake at that level to avoid a concentration of influence.
en.reason: Ahead of Anthropic’s IPO, Iconiq, Menlo and Lightspeed are the largest VC winners but each holds under 2%, a cap Anthropic set to stop any single investor from gaining concentrated influence after years of caution over governance and safety-first strategy.

en.summary: The PHP2Shell vulnerability was already being exploited by hackers four days before it was disclosed, with researchers at Calif and Wiz discovering the flaws. OpenAI says its frontier AI found the vulnerability before attackers did and worked with PHP, Calif, and Wiz to verify it and develop a patch. The NSA advises organizations unable to update immediately to take systems offline, while the UK's NCSC said the flaw could let hackers take control of web servers without login credentials. The White House said federal agencies are assessing the potential impact on government systems and critical infrastructure.
en.reason: Hackers exploited the PHP2Shell flaws four days before disclosure, and Wiz estimates the decade-old bugs — found by OpenAI and Google AI models — affect roughly 70% of websites, with the NSA urging immediate patching or going offline.

items.title: 一文讲透26年AI产品经理必懂的Agent分类
items.summary: AI Agent岗位越招越多，看着都叫“智能体”，背后的技术门槛、业务价值和职业风险却完全不同，选错方向，很可能刚转型就撞上大模型升级带来的淘汰。作者把编程、办公、深度研究、内容创作、流程自动化、客服、营销和行业 Agent 八条赛道逐一拆开，讲清了它们的运行逻辑、岗位需求与常见坑点。别只追最热概念，带上原有行业经验，去解决离业务和收入更近的问题，才更容易做出长期壁垒。

en.title: A Complete Guide to the Agent Classifications Every AI Product Manager Must Know in 2026
en.summary: AI Agent job postings keep multiplying, and they all look like "agents" on the surface—but the technical bar, business value, and career risk behind them are completely different. Pick the wrong track and you may barely finish your transition before the next LLM upgrade makes your role obsolete. The author breaks down eight tracks one by one—coding, office productivity, deep research, content creation, workflow automation, customer service, marketing, and industry-specific agents—explaining how each actually works, what the roles demand, and the common pitfalls. Don't just chase the hottest buzzword; bring your existing industry experience and solve problems closer to the business and revenue, and you'll be more likely to build a lasting moat.

en.title: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Value of CPUs: When Tokens Become Actions, the Compute Race Is No Longer Just About GPUs
en.summary:
Agentic AI is changing how CPU performance is judged.

Word count: 3,990 characters | Reading time: about 13 minutes

The center of gravity in AI infrastructure is shifting from raw GPU compute to end-to-end task execution, where CPUs and models work in concert. In Agent scenarios, tool calling, orchestration, and reasoning support are becoming the new yardsticks for CPU performance. Arm, together with Meta, OpenAI, and others, is pushing an evaluation paradigm that replaces Token throughput with task completion.

CPUs must support the model's "think–act" loop, not merely accelerate inference; toolchain latency and task orchestration efficiency determine an Agent's real productivity; and the division of compute is moving from GPU-centric to heterogeneous, collaborative architectures.

This is essential reading for AI infrastructure engineers, LLM systems architects, and cloud platform performance optimization engineers.

For the past two years, competition in AI infrastructure has revolved almost entirely around GPUs. How many Tokens a model can generate, how many Tokens it can output per second, and how much inference throughput it can sustain per watt have become key measures of compute efficiency.

But as AI Agents move from chat Q&A to software development, enterprise automation, and complex task execution, a new question is emerging: if a model generates code but takes a long time to compile and test it; if inference is fast enough but tool calling, database access, and task orchestration can't keep up, then...
en.reason: Arm, Meta and OpenAI are pushing to replace Token-throughput benchmarks with task-completion metrics for CPUs, as agent workloads shift tool calling, orchestration and the "think-act" loop onto the CPU and move infrastructure away from GPU-centric designs.

en.title: PostgreSQL 19 Delayed? AI Is Finding Bugs Faster Than Humans Can Fix Them
en.summary:
AI keeps finding problems without end — so how much should humans actually fix?

4,288 words | about 14 minutes to read

PostgreSQL 19 has been delayed after a large batch of fixes went insufficiently validated and nearly 10 features were withdrawn; an RC2 has been added to strengthen community testing. The root cause is not AI producing poor code, but LLM-driven automated review and fuzzing exposing deep, long-undetected flaws in legacy code ahead of schedule.

AI-assisted review has brought roughly five years' worth of latent defects to the surface all at once during Beta; the feature withdrawals stem mainly from edge-case and concurrency-logic flaws revealed by the new tools; the PostgreSQL release process is being forced to adapt to a shift in the quality-verification paradigm brought on by AI.

Intended for database kernel developers, open-source maintainers, and AI for Systems engineers.

Recently, the PostgreSQL 19 release hit a rare snag. The PostgreSQL team announced that PostgreSQL 19, originally scheduled for official release on October 29, will be pushed back to November 19. Before that, the project will add an extra release candidate, RC2, on November 12. The stated reason: a relatively large number of fixes have recently been added to the maintenance branches, and the team wants the community to validate them through RC2 before the official release.
en.reason: PostgreSQL 19's release slips from October 29 to November 19 with an added RC2 and 8–10 features withdrawn, as AI-driven review surfaces five-year-old defects faster than humans can fix them.

AI加速科学发现进程，尤其在物理学与生物医药领域具突破潜力；人类劳动价值正从执行转向定义问题与整合结果；创造快感与职业认同面临重构。

在 OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 看来，这已经不再是一个遥远的问题。随着 AI 开始参与真正的科学发现，人类正在进入一个新阶段。他预计，未来几年内，AI 有望帮助找到重大疾病的候选治疗方案。但相比医学进展，最让他个人感到兴奋的，反而是物理学领域可能出现的重大突破。

en.summary:
We've built ever-smarter AI—and we may lose the joy of solving hard problems."
"We've built ever-smarter AI—and we may lose the joy of solving hard problems."
Word count: 13,101
Reading time: about 43 minutes
AI is now deeply involved in mathematical proofs, the discovery of physical laws, and drug R&D—yet human workloads have not shrunk but grown. Roles like programmers are busier, more productive, and better paid as demand surges. Efficiency gains come alongside the erosion of joy in the creative process.
AI is accelerating scientific discovery, with breakthrough potential especially in physics and biomedicine. The value of human labor is shifting from execution toward defining problems and integrating results. Creative satisfaction and professional identity face reconstruction.
Suited for AI researchers, scientific computing engineers, and technology strategy decision-makers.
If one day AI could complete the most complex mathematical proofs, discover new laws of physics, or even find treatments for major diseases, what would humans still need to do?
For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, this is no longer a distant question. As AI begins to take part in real scientific discovery, humanity is entering a new phase. He expects that within a few years, AI could help find candidate treatments for major diseases. But compared with medical progress, what excites him most personally is the major breakthroughs that may emerge in physics.
But does stronger AI necessarily mean better lives for humans?
Recently, in a conversation with AI blogger Matthew

en.title: AI-powered development doubles Spotify's monthly code changes
en.summary:
Spotify expands AI-assisted development across its stack, with merged changes in August more than doubling year over year.

Word count: 1,089 | ~4 min read

Spotify is scaling AI-assisted development into production systems, with more than 17,000 merged changes in August, while reworking its quality and reliability controls to support high-concurrency scenarios.

The key problems centered on contention for content pipeline resources, bottlenecks in cluster automation governance, and mobile quality assurance; content delays were resolved through end-to-end monitoring, scheduler fixes, and priority refactoring; Honk (Claude Agent) and Fleetshift were brought in to work together on automated code changes and CI builds in Kubernetes environments.

Intended for platform engineers, SREs, and AI engineering teams.

Spotify has expanded the scope of AI-assisted development, with merged changes in August more than doubling year over year, from about 8,100 to 17,000. The company is reworking its quality and reliability controls to handle the surge in software changes across production systems.

Spotify runs nearly 3,000 production services supporting 777 million monthly active users, roughly 100 million concurrent clients, and 11 million to 12 million requests per second.
en.reason: Spotify's August merged changes more than doubled from about 8,100 to 17,000 as it scaled AI-assisted development with Honk and Fleetshift while reworking quality controls for nearly 3,000 production services.

en.title: Qwen's Jiang Guanjun: Building a Personal Agent tech framework requires coordinated progress across models, memory, and the ecosystem
en.summary:
Qwen places greater emphasis on task execution stability.

Word count: 947
Reading time: about 3 minutes

Qwen argues that a Personal Agent must coordinate three elements—model, memory, and ecosystem—to deliver personalized proactive service and create incremental value. AI is now moving from the agent stage to the assistant stage, with an emphasis on autonomous planning around user goals and the discovery of implicit needs. Its technical work focuses on task stability, long-term user understanding, and precise service across scenarios.

The model covers a demand map spanning 30+ industries, defines 8,000+ atomic capabilities, and incorporates expert evaluation; memory is stored in tiers according to the strength of event associations to avoid noise interference; ecosystem collaboration is the key path to unlocking 100% of the theoretical problem-solving potential.

Intended for AI architects, Agent system engineers, and LLM product leads.

On October 22, at the 2026 China Computer Congress, Jiang Guanjun, head of AI algorithms at Alibaba's Qwen business unit, shared Qwen's technical practice in building a Personal Agent. He argues that the true Personal Agent stage should create incremental value and personalized proactive service, and that model, memory, and ecosystem are the three elements that together build this core capability.

en.title: 20 pieces of AI industry jargon 🤖 Terms outsiders hear all the time but don't necessarily understand: Large model — a model with a huge parameter count, trained on massive amounts of data.
en.reason: Twenty AI jargon terms are decoded, from parameters—where "how many billion" signals scale, not intelligence—to tokens, which are neither fixed characters nor fixed words, and context windows holding chats, uploads and answers.

items.title: 很多人还在拿AI给老业务打补丁，看完曾鸣的最新演讲，直接刷新认知。他有个很震撼的判断： 当下的AI赛道，相当于1993年的互联网，基建就位，但标志性的“浏览器”还没诞生，真正的应用爆发还在加载，大家基本站在同一起跑线 先分清两个玩法：AI增强和AI原生。很多产品只是套了AI皮肤，拿掉AI照样运转；真正的AI原生项目，内核完全围绕智能搭建，去掉AI直接宕机。接下来Agent会逐步进化，从只会聊天，到动手干活，最终做到对结果负责，这才是通…

en.title: Plenty of people are still using AI to patch up their legacy businesses—Zeng Ming's latest talk will completely reset how you think about it.
en.reason: Zeng Ming argues today's AI sector mirrors the internet in 1993—infrastructure ready but no defining "browser" yet—and separates AI-enhanced products, which still run without AI, from AI-native ones that collapse without it, tracing Agent evolution from chat to taking responsibility for outcomes.

items.title: 近年来，大语言模型与 AI Agent 的快速发展，正在推动人工智能自主执行时代的到来。当 AI Agent 开始能够独立完成信息检索、服务调用、商业决策乃至商品购买时，支付便不再只是人与商户之间的交易行为，而是逐渐成为机器与机器之间价值交换的重要基础设施。全球支付体系因此也迎来了新的变革。 然而，支付智能化和支付全球化已经成为了一种必然的发展趋势。为了应对这些挑战，中国支付产业一方面持续优化传统支付基础设施，另一方面加速推进新型金融…

items.title: 一天用 Agent 适配 X-VLA，APXInf 在 4090 上表现如何？ 先说两个名字。 APXInf 是给机器人模型用的推理引擎。 机器人模型要看图、读指令、输出动作，又常跑在小设备或一张消费级显卡上，PyTorch 直接跑不够快。 APXInf 的做法是把底层算子和执行流程都优化过一遍，模型跑起来比框架直接跑快。 接新模型的时候，已有的算子可以复用，缺的计算和执行逻辑再补。 官方现在已经支持 π0.5、π0-FAST、GR0…

en.title: To take part in this AI economy, you shouldn't just be a user of AI — you should be a producer of AI.

en.title: UIUC, Google, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and CMU have jointly released a long survey paper, Proactive AI for Superintelligent Agents. Its main topic is the major pillars on the path to superintelligent agents; our current understanding is intelligence and alignment.
en.reason: A UIUC, Google, Stanford, UC Berkeley and CMU survey, Proactive AI for Superintelligent Agents, adds proactivity to intelligence and alignment as a pillar of superintelligent agents, tracing it to Wooldridge and Jennings' 1995 four agent traits and asking how LLM reactive interaction copes with tasks spanning days or weeks.

en.title:
iFlytek's open-source 4B small model: I tested it for a night on a computer with no GPU

On the afternoon of October 22, 2026, iFlytek released Spark X2.6 at its 1024 Developer Festival and simultaneously open-sourced the on-device small model Spark-X2.6-4B.
en.reason: iFlytek's Spark-X2.6-4B, posted to Hugging Face on October 21 under Apache 2.0, gets a hands-on night of testing on a graphics-card-free PC, alongside the 293B-parameter, 30B-activated, 1M-context Spark X2.6 cloud MoE.

en.title: ✨ Archify: turn any idea, plan, or codebase into a beautiful interactive architecture diagram in one click!
en.reason: Archify, an Agent Skill for Claude Code and Codex with 86k stars, turns any idea, plan or codebase into an interactive architecture diagram, using a typed JSON IR and atomic pre-delivery validation so shared endpoints spread deterministically instead of piling arrows on one midpoint.

en.title: A Complete Guide to the Agent Classifications Every AI Product Manager Must Know in 2026
en.summary: AI Agent job postings keep multiplying, and they all look like "agents" on the surface—but the technical bar, business value, and career risk behind them are completely different. Pick the wrong track and you may barely finish your transition before the next LLM upgrade makes your role obsolete. The author breaks down eight tracks one by one—coding, office productivity, deep research, content creation, workflow automation, customer service, marketing, and industry-specific agents—explaining how each actually works, what the roles demand, and the common pitfalls. Don't just chase the hottest buzzword; bring your existing industry experience and solve problems closer to the business and revenue, and you'll be more likely to build a lasting moat.
en.reason: Eight Agent tracks—coding, office, deep research, content creation, process automation, customer service, marketing and industry—are broken down by logic, hiring demand and pitfalls, citing Cursor and Claude Code's self-debugging workflows and warning against base-model R&D.

en.title: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Value of CPUs: When Tokens Become Actions, the Compute Race Is No Longer Just About GPUs
en.summary:
Agentic AI is changing how CPU performance is judged.

Word count: 3,990 characters | Reading time: about 13 minutes

The center of gravity in AI infrastructure is shifting from raw GPU compute to end-to-end task execution, where CPUs and models work in concert. In Agent scenarios, tool calling, orchestration, and reasoning support are becoming the new yardsticks for CPU performance. Arm, together with Meta, OpenAI, and others, is pushing an evaluation paradigm that replaces Token throughput with task completion.

CPUs must support the model's "think–act" loop, not merely accelerate inference; toolchain latency and task orchestration efficiency determine an Agent's real productivity; and the division of compute is moving from GPU-centric to heterogeneous, collaborative architectures.

This is essential reading for AI infrastructure engineers, LLM systems architects, and cloud platform performance optimization engineers.

For the past two years, competition in AI infrastructure has revolved almost entirely around GPUs. How many Tokens a model can generate, how many Tokens it can output per second, and how much inference throughput it can sustain per watt have become key measures of compute efficiency.

But as AI Agents move from chat Q&A to software development, enterprise automation, and complex task execution, a new question is emerging: if a model generates code but takes a long time to compile and test it; if inference is fast enough but tool calling, database access, and task orchestration can't keep up, then...
en.reason: Arm, Meta and OpenAI are pushing to replace Token-throughput benchmarks with task-completion metrics for CPUs, as agent workloads shift tool calling, orchestration and the "think-act" loop onto the CPU and move infrastructure away from GPU-centric designs.

en.title: PostgreSQL 19 Delayed? AI Is Finding Bugs Faster Than Humans Can Fix Them
en.summary:
AI keeps finding problems without end — so how much should humans actually fix?

4,288 words | about 14 minutes to read

PostgreSQL 19 has been delayed after a large batch of fixes went insufficiently validated and nearly 10 features were withdrawn; an RC2 has been added to strengthen community testing. The root cause is not AI producing poor code, but LLM-driven automated review and fuzzing exposing deep, long-undetected flaws in legacy code ahead of schedule.

AI-assisted review has brought roughly five years' worth of latent defects to the surface all at once during Beta; the feature withdrawals stem mainly from edge-case and concurrency-logic flaws revealed by the new tools; the PostgreSQL release process is being forced to adapt to a shift in the quality-verification paradigm brought on by AI.

Intended for database kernel developers, open-source maintainers, and AI for Systems engineers.

Recently, the PostgreSQL 19 release hit a rare snag. The PostgreSQL team announced that PostgreSQL 19, originally scheduled for official release on October 29, will be pushed back to November 19. Before that, the project will add an extra release candidate, RC2, on November 12. The stated reason: a relatively large number of fixes have recently been added to the maintenance branches, and the team wants the community to validate them through RC2 before the official release.
en.reason: PostgreSQL 19's release slips from October 29 to November 19 with an added RC2 and 8–10 features withdrawn, as AI-driven review surfaces five-year-old defects faster than humans can fix them.

en.title: AI-powered development doubles Spotify's monthly code changes
en.summary:
Spotify expands AI-assisted development across its stack, with merged changes in August more than doubling year over year.

Word count: 1,089 | ~4 min read

Spotify is scaling AI-assisted development into production systems, with more than 17,000 merged changes in August, while reworking its quality and reliability controls to support high-concurrency scenarios.

The key problems centered on contention for content pipeline resources, bottlenecks in cluster automation governance, and mobile quality assurance; content delays were resolved through end-to-end monitoring, scheduler fixes, and priority refactoring; Honk (Claude Agent) and Fleetshift were brought in to work together on automated code changes and CI builds in Kubernetes environments.

Intended for platform engineers, SREs, and AI engineering teams.

Spotify has expanded the scope of AI-assisted development, with merged changes in August more than doubling year over year, from about 8,100 to 17,000. The company is reworking its quality and reliability controls to handle the surge in software changes across production systems.

Spotify runs nearly 3,000 production services supporting 777 million monthly active users, roughly 100 million concurrent clients, and 11 million to 12 million requests per second.

en.title: Qwen's Jiang Guanjun: Building a Personal Agent tech framework requires coordinated progress across models, memory, and the ecosystem
en.summary:
Qwen places greater emphasis on task execution stability.

Word count: 947
Reading time: about 3 minutes

Qwen argues that a Personal Agent must coordinate three elements—model, memory, and ecosystem—to deliver personalized proactive service and create incremental value. AI is now moving from the agent stage to the assistant stage, with an emphasis on autonomous planning around user goals and the discovery of implicit needs. Its technical work focuses on task stability, long-term user understanding, and precise service across scenarios.

The model covers a demand map spanning 30+ industries, defines 8,000+ atomic capabilities, and incorporates expert evaluation; memory is stored in tiers according to the strength of event associations to avoid noise interference; ecosystem collaboration is the key path to unlocking 100% of the theoretical problem-solving potential.

Intended for AI architects, Agent system engineers, and LLM product leads.

On October 22, at the 2026 China Computer Congress, Jiang Guanjun, head of AI algorithms at Alibaba's Qwen business unit, shared Qwen's technical practice in building a Personal Agent. He argues that the true Personal Agent stage should create incremental value and personalized proactive service, and that model, memory, and ecosystem are the three elements that together build this core capability.

Jiang divides the evolution of AI applications into three stages: conversation, agent, and assistant. Today, AI applications are accelerating toward the assistant stage, and on top of delivering concrete tasks, they are beginning to combine professional experience and individual...

en.title: Plenty of people are still using AI to patch up their legacy businesses—Zeng Ming's latest talk will completely reset how you think about it.
en.reason: Zeng Ming argues today's AI sector mirrors the internet in 1993—infrastructure ready but no defining "browser" yet—and separates AI-enhanced products, which still run without AI, from AI-native ones that collapse without it, tracing Agent evolution from chat to taking responsibility for outcomes.
